name: Almost Black
lede: Almost Black names a near-black that writers have reached for across centuries to describe shadows, snow-dark water and over-saturated paint, though the exact name was only logged as a color term in a 2010 crowd survey.

sections.title: A modifier, not a pigment
sections.body:
"Almost" is a modifier word, not a material: it says this shade sits just short of true black rather than naming a dye, mineral or place [1]. Paterson's dictionary lists the modifier itself, noting it is used in descriptions such as "almost black" and "almost white," most often for flowers [1]. ColorHub's library first catalogs the exact name Almost Black from the 2010 xkcd crowd survey; who coined it as a fixed color term is otherwise undocumented [2].

The phrase is old as plain description, though, long before any survey. Writers on color and painting use it for a water stream next to bright snow, for cherries fading at dusk, and for green foliage darkened by decayed resin in old pictures [3]. The nearest named neighbors are [[rich-black-fogra39|Rich Black FOGRA39]] and [[smoky-black]] [4].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: This is one of the most common tones in our archive: it appears in 15.15 percent of 23,781 paintings (3,604 of them, as photographed), more common than 99 percent of the named colors here [5]. Inside a painting it most often plays a shadow, found that way in 77 percent of the 3,192 paintings where it is the dominant local color [5]. It peaks in paintings from the 1600s, at 1.2 times the expected rate for that century, and shares canvases with [[blood-red|Blood Red]] and [[black-bean|Black Bean]] more than chance [5]. The earliest matching canvas dates to the year 1000, a thousand years before the exact name was recorded in 2010; the archive's early centuries are thin, so this is a floor, not a first, and that distance is a look-alike hue, not proof any painter used this name [5].

origin.named_after: undocumented as a fixed color term; the modifier "almost" plus "black" is old descriptive usage

questions.q: What role does Almost Black most often play inside a painting in our archive?
True or false: a 1000 CE painting matching this color proves painters already called it Almost Black.

openers: Almost Black plays a shadow in more than three-quarters of the paintings where it appears.

issues: No single coiner or date for the exact term; distinguished the old descriptive phrase from the 2010 survey record.
